text:
Maya: FYI rolling a change that refactors the 'private_admin' RBAC bindings into a more granular set landed in staging 10m ago. I noticed in Dedicated clusters a user with only 'workload_deploy' perms was able to view control-plane logs. not good. can someone triage?
Jared: on it. any repro steps? which cluster id?
Maya: cluster:d-7893 in staging. repro: 1) user with role workload_deploy opened the controlplane UI 2) they could see /audit/logs (should be private_admin only)
Priya: can you paste the policy snippet that was applied? might be a merge bug between allowlists and role bindings.
Maya: paste below:
```
roles:
  - name: workload_deploy
    allow: [deploy:create, deploy:list]
  - name: private_admin
    allow: [controlplane:read, controlplane:write, kms:decrypt]
bindings:
  - subject: group:staging-developers
    role: workload_deploy
  - subject: group:onprem-admins
    role: private_admin
```
Jared: looks ok at first glance. what did the audit log show when the user accessed /audit/logs?
Maya: from audit service:
```
{"time":"2026-03-18T16:12:23Z","user":"okta|u-342","subject":"ui.controlplane.logs","result":"allowed","policy_evals":["binding:group:onprem-admins","flag:allow_vpc_bypass"]}
```
Priya: oh `flag:allow_vpc_bypass` is set via the VPC allowlist plugin. that flag should only be applied for network-level exemptions, not RBAC. if that plugin mutated the eval context to add extra bindings that's the bug.
sec-bot: ALERT: policy-eval-anomaly detected for cluster:d-7893 by user okta|u-342. Correlation id: 56f3a2.
ops-oncall: saw a flurry of related alerts around 16:10; believed to be a noisy test but reopening.
Leo: possible root cause: recent change in plugin dispatcher (PR #3487) now runs allowlist plugins before RBAC merge and they can inject ephemeral subjects. PR moves plugin order; maybe it accidentally grants `group:onprem-admins` as an ephemeral subject when the VPC allowlist matches.
Jared: can we confirm whether the ephemeral subject was logged? look for `ephemeral_subject:` fields in the policy trace.
Maya: policy trace snippet:
```
- eval_step: vpc_allowlist
  matched: true
  ephemeral_subject: group:onprem-admins
- eval_step: rbac_merge
  merged_bindings: [workload_deploy, ephemeral:group:onprem-admins]
```
Priya: yep ephemeral subject clearly injected. mitigation: revert PR #3487 or change the dispatcher to mark ephemeral subjects as non-binding for control-plane resources.
Jared: mitigation plan: 1) hotfix dispatcher to not add ephemeral subjects to merge context 2) push emergency rollback of PR #3487 to staging and prod rollback window 3) run full audit to enumerate affected requests 4) rotate any service tokens that used `kms:decrypt` during the window
Maya: estimating blast window ~ 16:05-16:18 UTC. I will open an incident and assign follow-ups.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-203. Assigned: Maya, Jared, Priya.
Priya: I'll take the hotfix. Jared take audit enumeration. Maya coordinate rollback and incident timeline.
Leo: adding note: for Private deployments we should ensure onprem-admins mapping is gated behind a KMS-wrapped attestation (don't allow ephemeral injection to masquerade).
Maya: agreed. will add to postmortem. thanks all :thumbsup:
